name: Ratio Calendar Spread (Front Ratio Time Spread)
summary: Sell more near-term contracts than the longer-dated contracts bought at the same strike, usually 2:1, financing the calendar into a credit or free structure at the cost of a naked short.
max_profit: Achieved with spot at the strike at front expiry: both shorts expire worthless and the long back-month retains its time value. Approximately (back-month value at front expiry) + net credit.
max_loss: UNDEFINED on the call version above the strike (one short is uncovered) and (strike x 100 x 1 - credit) on the put version below the strike. The excess short is naked by construction.
breakevens: Upside breakeven approximately strike + (max profit at the strike)/100 for the 2:1 call version; downside limited to the debit paid or improved by the credit received.

greeks.delta: negative for the 2:1 call version above the strike; near zero at the strike
greeks.gamma: strongly negative (two shorts against one long)
greeks.vega: can be near zero or negative depending on the ratio - the second short offsets the back month's vega

when_to_use: IV rank 30-60 with a firm expectation that the underlying pins or drifts slightly against the excess short. Occasionally used to finance a back-month long for free. Given the naked leg, it is a level-4 structure and is included mainly for completeness.
entry_rules: REQUIRES ALPACA OPTIONS LEVEL 4 - only one of the two short fronts is covered by the single back-month long; the second is naked. The automation must reject this at level 3. A level-3-legal alternative is to add a further OTM long front-month option, turning it into a covered ratio (see calendar-backspread for the level-3 inverse).
Ratio never worse than 2:1; 3:1 is prohibited by policy.
Front shorts by delta 0.30-0.45; long back at the identical strike.
Net credit >= $0 (never pay a debit for a structure that carries a naked leg).
Size on the naked-leg margin for the uncovered contract.
management_rules: Close at +50% of max theoretical profit or +50% of credit, whichever applies.
Stop at 2x the credit received, or if the naked side's |delta| exceeds 0.50.
Close the excess short immediately if spot trades through the strike.
exit_rules: Close or roll ALL short legs by 14:30 ET on front expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the excess (uncovered) short the moment spot touches the strike - do not wait for the delta or time trigger.
Close any short whose extrinsic <= $0.05 or |delta| >= 0.90.
Short calls: close before ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share.
Buy back shorts before selling the long.
assignment_risk: Two short front-month contracts, only one of which has a same-strike back-month cover. If both are assigned, the account is short 200 shares against one long call - a genuinely uncovered position that must be flattened immediately. This is the reason the structure is level 4 and is discouraged.
buying_power: Covered pair requires the debit; the uncovered contract requires full naked margin (greater of 20% of underlying value minus OTM amount or 10% of underlying value, plus premium).
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 both expiries; must be closeable in one order.
common_mistakes: Selling the extra contract for a few cents of credit and taking on unlimited risk; assuming the back-month long 'sort of' covers both shorts (it does not); running the ratio on a name that can gap.
zero_dte_notes: Absolutely not - a naked 0DTE short on a share-settled underlying is the single worst assignment profile available.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
